transcript: The writer/director team that brought us The Ferryman has done it again. In this new play called The Hills of California, three sisters in England reconvene at their childhood home while their mother is dying. The fourth sister has been out of the picture for 20 years so everyone's wondering if she'll even show up. This is the starting point from which we see how resentment and lost dreams plague the sisters, and we jump back and forth between the 70s and the 50s to see how everything unfolded and the way it fractured their family. It’s actually a simple story and a bit of a slow burn which makes it rather understated but grounded in what I felt was good writing, great performances, and amazing direction. Jez Butterworth’s script is lyrical and precise and the direction by Sam Mendes is natural and gorgeously leverages the stunning set design. For performances, the entire cast is great but probably most memorable is Laura Donnelly's complex and damaged Veronica, the mother of the four sisters who is deeply committed to championing a dream for herself and her daughters but who is also deeply flawed. I think the comparison to The Ferryman is pretty inevitable, with this being another Butterworth/Mendes collaboration on a big three act family story but I think they're quite different. I feel this play doesn't have the big shocking moments like The Ferryman does, and it's perhaps not as inventive, but on the other hand I appreciated how this play was still quite captivating and was able to achieve that through a set of very ordinary characters. I do think the run time will be a bit long for some folks but I personally liked having the time to really sit with the characters and buy into the emotional stakes. It didn't feel that long to me. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
